head: 418cc8e4c127911a10fb740e899c0e83acaeb555
summary:
At HEAD 418cc8e, every acceptance criterion I could reach holds against the real Windows Explorer on this desktop, and nothing I measured failed. Criterion 12 failed last time and now holds. Criterion 3 is not fully checked because its \\server\share root case could not be reached here.

**The fix from last time.** I checked criterion 12 with my own probe startup hook in %TEMP%, which never writes the menu's Tag or CommandTarget, on the published exe during a live scan of 60,000 folders:
- The results-list row's container detached ({DisconnectedItem}) 142–158 ms after the menu opened, and 5 more refreshes followed.
- The entry stayed enabled. At the click the scan was still running, and the app's own capture revealed that row Exact.
- Explorer showed live\ with exactly a7 selected (1 item).
- A second row's menu, which has its own instance, captured and revealed a2 while the scan was still running.

**R-001, B-007 and B-008 all passed.** R-001 now requires the app itself to capture the row, closes the windows it opened before every step, and includes the new top-live step. B-007 and B-008 now prove the status line was on screen and one line tall (status=True, 15.96 px).

**Other real checks this run:**
- **Largest-files list, via the menu:** the file was selected, and it was the only item selected.
- **Largest-files list, via Ctrl+Enter:** I set Ctrl in the app thread's own keyboard state and sent a KeyDown to the focused row, so the command's own Ctrl+Enter gesture fired it. The file was selected.
- **633-character path from the window's own row:** Exact, and selected.
- **File deleted after the scan, at the 560 px minimum width:**
  - The reveal climbed to its folder (Ancestor / NoLongerExists), and Explorer selected that folder in its parent.
  - The status line stayed one line (15.96 px). Its lead words "No longer exists, so highlighting" fit (174 of 512 px).
- **Unreachable share, seen inside the window:** the call returned after 42.1 s as Failed 0x80070043 and did not climb. The status read "Couldn't open Explorer: The network name cannot be found (0x80070043). '…'". The UI thread never took more than 1 ms to respond.
- **Second reveal while the first was still pending:** the local reveal landed Exact at 0.6 s, and its outcome was still on screen at 60.9 s, after the slow share call would have returned.
- **Names the shell mis-parses** (through Core's RevealAsync, the call the window makes): 'sp ', 'con', 'nul.txt' and 'dir.\in.txt' each landed on their folder, selected in its parent. The decoy 'sp' was never selected.
- **Drive root C:\:** Explorer opened This PC with 'OS (C:)' selected.
- **A drive letter that does not exist (Q:):** Failed 0x8007000F, with no window.
- **A folder whose listing was denied after the scan** (my own temp folder): Failed 0x80004004, with no climb and no window.
- **An Explorer window already open on the folder:** it was reused, and its selection was replaced by exactly the new item.

**Base checks:** build 0 warnings, 296 Core tests passed (36 of them ShellReveal), all 47 fitness rules hold.

**What is not met or still open:**
- **Criterion 3, the \\server\share root:** only Plan's unit test covers it. There is no share to try it on without creating SMB client mappings or reading network configuration, and I left alone Z:, which is a mapped network drive of the person's. A person should either try it on a real share or accept the unit test.
- **Ctrl+Enter on a results-list row during a live scan:** it works on the row as it stands. After the next refresh, focus falls to the ListBox, CanExecute is false, and the key press does nothing. It never acts on a wrong row. With refreshes every 250 ms, a person will effectively never manage it mid-scan. build-slice already recorded this as needing a design decision. It is not one of the 14 criteria.
- **O-001 is still open on the ledger.** The behaviour holds and R-001 step 1 feeds exactly that shape, but no discharge command was ever named for it. build-slice should name `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case R-001`.

**Loop check:** this is not a loop. Build attempts 4–6 were a provider quota error (429) and a lost process, and changed nothing. Attempt 7 changed src and fixed the defect.

All my temp trees, logs and the Explorer windows I opened were removed, and the working tree is unchanged.

checks.what: R-001 reveal matrix through the published exe and real Explorer
checks.evidence: PASSED: R-001, every line ok. The app's Opened handler captured the row on every menu step. Before each step the windows the case opened were closed, with 0 left. dup. ran before the root step, its folder reveal-root was selected, and the decoy was never selected in the 2 s poll. top-live logged captured, detached, sentinel, scanning, enabled and open all true, kind Exact, and the row selected in Explorer. The placeholder step logged found, captured and disabled.

checks.what: B-007 minimum-size layout with the status line shown
checks.evidence: PASSED: B-007. 'the reveal status line was on screen, one line of 15.96 px' (status=True statusHeight=15.96) in both variants

checks.evidence: PASSED: B-008, status=True statusHeight=15.96

checks.what: Own probe: results-list row menu during a live 60k-folder scan. The probe never writes Tag or CommandTarget. The first row is clicked after refreshes have detached its container, then a second row is opened
checks.evidence: At open: tagIsRow=true, cmdTargetIsWindow=true, scanning=true. After a refresh: detached=true at 158 ms, then 5 refreshes in the next 1.5 s, containerDC={DisconnectedItem}, enabledAtClick=true, scanningAtClick=true, outcome Exact live\a1, scanningAtOutcome=true. Row 2: tagIsRow2=true, sameMenuInstanceAsRow1=false, Exact live\a2 while still scanning.

checks.what: Own probe: a single live-scan reveal (a7), then Explorer read through Shell.Application
checks.evidence: detached at 142 ms, 5 refreshes, enabledAtClick=true, scanningAtClick=true, Exact. Explorer: 'MATCH after 34 ms: window=[...\live] selectedCount=1 selected=a7'

checks.what: Own probe: Ctrl+Enter during a live scan on the focused row, while attached. VK_CONTROL is set in the app UI thread's keyboard state, then KeyDown(Enter) is raised so the command's own gesture fires it
checks.evidence: windowActive=true, focusedIsContainer=true, modifiersSeen=Control, outcome Exact live\a3, and Explorer selected a3 (count 1). Afterwards modifiers were restored to None.

checks.what: Own probe: Ctrl+Enter on the same results-list row after a live refresh detached it
checks.evidence: detached=true, scanning=true, focus had moved to the ListBox (focusedDC=null), canExecute=false, and the press gave no new outcome. No wrong target was acted on. This is build-slice's recorded open item and needs a design decision. It is not one of the 14 criteria.

checks.what: Own probe: largest-files row via the menu after completion, checking the selection is exactly one item (O-001's shape)
checks.evidence: tagIsRow=true, enabled=true, Exact. Explorer: 'window=[...\small] selectedCount=1 selected=largest.bin'

checks.what: Own probe: Ctrl+Enter on a largest-files row after completion
checks.evidence: focusedIsContainer=true, modifiersSeen=Control, keyTarget=ListBoxItem, Exact near.bin. Explorer selectedCount=1 near.bin

checks.what: Own probe: a 633-character path revealed from the window's largest-files row
checks.evidence: rowPathLength=633 (display form), Exact hr=0. Explorer window on the parent in 8.3 form, selectedCount=1, six_hundred.bin|SIX_HU~1.BIN

checks.what: Own probe: file deleted after the scan, revealed from its row at the 560 px minimum width, with the status line measured
checks.evidence: Ancestor/NoLongerExists, Shown = the parent folder. Explorer showed the grandparent with that folder selected (count 1). Status: 'No longer exists, so highlighting '<parent>' instead: '<file>''. windowWidth=560, statusActualHeight=15.96, statusActualWidth=512, full text 2858 px (trimmed), lead words 174 px, so statusLeadFits=true.

checks.what: Own probe: reveal of the unreachable \\192.0.2.1\share\far.txt, observed inside the window
checks.evidence: The status read 'Opening in Explorer…' at once. The app's own call returned at 42096 ms: Failed hr=0x80070043, shown=null (no climb). Status: 'Couldn't open Explorer: The network name cannot be found (0x80070043). '\\192.0.2.1\share\far.txt'', one line at 15.96 px. maxUiRoundTripMs=0.

checks.what: Own probe: a second reveal 200 ms after the unreachable one
checks.evidence: near.bin Exact at 599 ms. LastRevealOutcome and the status were unchanged in all 30 samples from 2.6 s to 60.9 s, past the 42.1 s at which the far call returns. maxUiRoundTripMs=1. Explorer selectedCount=1 near.bin

checks.what: Drive root C:\ through Core ShellReveal.RevealAsync, the call the window makes
checks.evidence: Kind=Exact hr=0x00000000 in 314 ms. The window was 'This PC' with 'OS (C:)<C:\>' selected. I closed only that window.

checks.what: Names the shell mis-parses, real, through Core RevealAsync: 'sp ' with a decoy 'sp', 'con', 'nul.txt', 'dir.\in.txt'
checks.command: RevealAsync(%TEMP%\sl047-val2\odd\<name>), then a 2 s poll of every Explorer window
checks.evidence: Each gave Ancestor/NameUnaddressable. The bad names were 'sp ', 'con', 'nul.txt' and 'dir.'. Each time the only window was sl047-val2 with 'odd' selected (count 1), and decoyEverSelected=False.

checks.what: A real access-denied case: the parent folder's listing denied (icacls /deny RD on my own temp folder) after the file existed
checks.evidence: Failed hr=0x80004004 (E_ABORT, 'Operation aborted'), Shown empty, so no climb. No Explorer window and no dialog left behind. The deny was removed afterwards. It is not E_ACCESSDENIED, but it is handled the same way: Failed, with no climb.

checks.what: Whole chain gone, on a drive letter that does not exist
checks.evidence: Failed hr=0x8007000F in 20 ms, Shown empty, no Explorer window. The real code is ERROR_INVALID_DRIVE, not the 0x80070003 the unit test fakes.

checks.what: Reveal into an Explorer window already open on the folder with another item selected
checks.command: RevealAsync(small\largest.bin), wait until it is selected, then RevealAsync(small\near.bin)
checks.evidence: After the second call there was one window (reused) with sel=near.bin only.

checks.what: Revealing a \\server\share root, or any item on a reachable share
checks.evidence: There is no share I may use. The SMB loopback rig creates SMB client mappings. Listing shares or reading where the person's mapped Z: points is network configuration. I did not touch Z:.

checks.what: An OS-level mouse right-click and a physical Ctrl+Enter
checks.evidence: Menus were opened the way ContextMenuService opens them (PlacementTarget, then IsOpen) and clicked through MenuItem.OnClick. The key was delivered in-process (thread keyboard state plus a routed KeyDown), not through SendInput. Driving the window from outside is off-limits here.

checks.what: Cleanup of my temp trees, probe, logs and Explorer windows
checks.evidence: sl047-val2 exists after: False. Explorer windows: 0. No FsAnalyser.App process was running. git status is unchanged (only the .taad records that were already modified). The command exited 1 only because Get-Process found no process.

criteria.criterion: 1. Open a file from the largest-files list in Explorer (LargestFileRow.Path)
criteria.how: R-001 step 1 passed, going through the menu with the app's own capture. My probe: the menu reveal gave Explorer selectedCount=1 largest.bin, and Ctrl+Enter through the command's gesture gave selectedCount=1 near.bin.

criteria.criterion: 2. Open a folder from the folder tree (non-root row, full path from ScanStore.GetPath)
criteria.how: R-001 real: 'subfolder' (depth 1) was selected in its parent. Tree rows whose path comes from GetPath resolved exactly at depth 2 (subfolder\inner.bin, selected) and depth 4 (a 322-character long_file.bin, selected). A folder at depth 2 or more was not itself revealed from the tree: the GetPath part is measured on files at depth, and folder selection on folders at depth 1 (subfolder, sym_dir, and the results-list folders a1–a7).

criteria.criterion: 3. Open the scan root: the tree root row, a drive root 'C:\', a \\server\share root
criteria.how: Tree root row: real, R-001 step 4 (reveal-root selected in its parent, path not doubled). C:\: real through Core RevealAsync, the call the window makes (This PC with 'OS (C:)' selected), but not from a C:\ tree root row, which needs a full scan of C:. \\server\share root: only Plan_RootShapes / Plan_PrefixesStripped unit tests; where Explorer lands is unmeasured because there is no share.

criteria.criterion: 4. Open an item with a very long path (~300 and ~600 characters, \\?\ stripped)
criteria.how: About 300: R-001 step 10, 322 characters from a tree row, Exact and selected. About 600: my probe revealed a 633-character display-form path from the window's largest-files row, Exact, with the file selected in its parent (8.3 form). Prefix stripping: Plan_PrefixesStripped.

criteria.criterion: 5. Open an item whose path holds a name the shell mis-parses
criteria.how: dup. through the app (R-001): Ancestor/NameUnaddressable, reveal-root selected, decoy never selected over 2 s. 'sp ' (decoy 'sp'), 'con', 'nul.txt' and 'dir.\in.txt' through Core RevealAsync: each Ancestor/NameUnaddressable with the folder selected in its parent, and the decoy never selected. 'COM¹' and 'CONIN$' are covered by unit tests only.

criteria.criterion: 6. Open an item with an unusual but addressable name
criteria.how: R-001 real: ' lead', 'a,b;c.txt', '%TEMP%.txt', 'dup' and '😀.txt' each Exact and selected in Explorer.

criteria.criterion: 7. Open an item deleted after the scan (parent exists; separately, the whole chain gone)
criteria.how: Parent exists: real through the window. gone.bin was deleted after the scan and gave Ancestor/NoLongerExists, with the parent selected in the grandparent and the status leading with 'No longer exists'. Whole chain gone: real through Core RevealAsync on the absent drive Q: gave Failed 0x8007000F, with no window and no climb. It was also covered by Walk_EntireChainDeleted_ReturnsFailed.

criteria.criterion: 8. Open a hidden or hidden+system item
criteria.how: R-001 step 5: hs_file.sys (Hidden+System) Exact, and the status note shown ('is hidden, so Explorer only highlights it if…'). As the design says, whether it is selected depends on Explorer settings and is not asserted. Explorer at its default hidden settings is not reached.

criteria.criterion: 9. Open a junction or symbolic link entry (to a file and to a folder)
criteria.how: R-001 steps 6–8 with real links (Developer Mode): junc, sym_file.bin and sym_dir each Exact, with the link itself selected in its parent.

criteria.criterion: 10. Handle a failing shell call that is not 'not found'
criteria.how: Real in the window: the unreachable share gave Failed 0x80070043 after 42.1 s with no climb, and a one-line status that leads with the outcome. The UI thread was never blocked. Real denial on my own temp folder: Failed 0x80004004 with no climb and no window. A literal E_ACCESSDENIED from the shell was not produced. Walk_AccessDeniedOrNetworkError_StopsWithoutClimbing covers 0x80070005 and 0x80070035.

criteria.criterion: 11. Open from the context menu on a tree row other than the selected one, including a nested row
criteria.how: R-001 step 11: the root row is selected, then the menu on nested inner.bin is opened. The app's own handler captured it (captured=true), and inner.bin was selected in Explorer. No physical mouse right-click was used.

criteria.criterion: 12. Open from the unreadable-folders list and from top-level rows (during a running scan, or after a stop or failure)
criteria.how: Unreadable list: R-001 step 14, a clean path, and denied selected in Explorer. Top-level rows during a running scan: my own probe, which does not write Tag, and R-001 top-live. After refreshes detached the container, the entry stayed enabled, the scan was running at the click, the reveal was Exact, and Explorer selected a7 (count 1). A second row's menu revealed its own row. After a stop: R-001 top step. After a failure was not run separately.

criteria.criterion: 13. Offer the command on a row that has no path
criteria.how: R-001 step 13 drew a real placeholder container and opened its RowContextMenu: found, captured and disabled all true. KindsList has no ContextMenu setter (MainWindow.xaml:480; only lines 317, 343, 393 and 424 set RowContextMenu). The Plan_EmptyOrWhitespace and Plan_InvalidOrRelativeInput unit tests pass.

criteria.criterion: 14. Start a second reveal before the first returns (the first slower, an unreachable share)
criteria.how: My probe in the window: far, then near 200 ms later. Near landed Exact at 0.6 s and stayed the outcome and status through 60.9 s. In the same app the far call returns at 42.1 s (far-alone run), so its late result was discarded. The UI thread's round trip never went above 1 ms.

obligations.evidence: Behaviour measured by my own probe: from the largest-files row's menu, Explorer shows the parent with selectedCount=1 = largest.bin within 33 ms. R-001 step 1 feeds exactly this shape and passed this run, but its Wait-ExplorerSelection checks that the file is among the selected items, not that it is the only one. It is still open on the ledger because no discharge command was ever named. build-slice should name `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case R-001`.

MainWindow.xaml.cs:721-724 sets CommandTarget = this and captures the row, or NoRow, into Tag. Measured live with my probe: container {DisconnectedItem}, enabledAtClick=true, scanningAtClick=true, Exact a7, and Explorer selected a7.
R-001 output: 'the Explorer windows the case opened are closed before the next step (0 left)' before every step. dup. runs before tree:root, and the decoy poll passed.
RevealMode.cs only reads menu.Tag (lines 184, 248 and 312) and never writes it. My own probe, which writes nothing, saw tagIsRow=true from the app's own Opened handler.
B-007 and B-008 both print status=True statusHeight=15.96 and assert 'the reveal status line was on screen, one line of 15.96 px'.
RevealMode.cs:48-50: WaitForScanToStart, then WaitForTopRow, then StopScan. The R-001 top step passed.

The Failed and NoLongerExists texts lead with the outcome. Measured at 560 px: the lead words take 174 of 512 px, and the line is 15.96 px tall. Real Failed text: 'Couldn't open Explorer: The network name cannot be found (0x80070043). '…''.

MainWindow.xaml.cs:724 uses ReferenceEquals(row, BindingOperations.DisconnectedSource) and maps it, or a null row, to NoRow, for which PathOf gives an empty path. The probe saw the sentinel at runtime (sentinel=true). The NoRow branch itself was not triggered, because a menu cannot be opened on an already-detached container.

not_reached: Revealing a \\server\share root, or any item on a reachable SMB share. There is no share I may use: the loopback rig creates SMB client mappings, and the person's mapped Z: was left alone. Only Plan's unit tests cover the UNC root.
C:\ from the window's own tree root row. That needs a full scan of C:. C:\ was revealed through Core's RevealAsync, the call the window makes.

A physical mouse right-click and a physical Ctrl+Enter. Menus were opened as ContextMenuService opens them, and the key was delivered in-process (thread keyboard state plus a routed KeyDown), not through SendInput.

Ctrl+Enter on a results-list row during a live scan works only until the next refresh (≤250 ms). After that, focus is on the ListBox and the press does nothing. Measured, not a wrong target. It needs the design decision build-slice recorded.

Explorer at Windows' default hidden settings (Hidden=2, ShowSuperHidden=0). This machine is at Hidden=1, and registry settings are off-limits. Only the hidden note is checked, not whether hidden or system items get selected.

A literal E_ACCESSDENIED (0x80070005) from SHParseDisplayName or SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems. The real denial produced E_ABORT (0x80004004), and the real network failure was 0x80070043, not 0x80070035.
A real removable or network volume disappearing mid-session. This was simulated with a never-present drive letter, giving 0x8007000F rather than the 0x80070003 the unit test fakes.
A machine with LongPathsEnabled=0. The 633-character reveal was measured only here, with LongPathsEnabled=1 and 8.3 names on C:.
A folder, rather than a file, at depth 2 or more revealed from the tree. GetPath was checked at depth on files, and folder selection on folders at depth 1.
Display scaling other than 100% for the one-line status budget (24 px) and the 644 px minimum height.
